one_line: Collaborative agent-assisted movie and TV discovery and lineup planning.
what_it_does: Lets a person explore titles, filter availability, save a watchlist, and maintain an ordered movie-night or weekend lineup with an agent while preserving human locks and exclusions.
leverage_rationale: Structured title search, streaming availability, lineup mutation, and human constraints make the agent a reliable collaborator rather than a scraper; general UI driving could approximate it but with meaningful friction.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes structured filters, watchlists, ordered lineups, locks, exclusions, and rebuilding only remaining picks.
Frame-sheet evidence was unavailable due to image-service rate limiting; packet authoritatively marks video present.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is coherent and unusually complete for a recommendation product, though the available visual evidence did not verify the end-to-end lineup flow.
execution_evidence: Detailed product description covers discovery, title detail, trailer/availability, watchlist, lineup, and constraint-aware revision.
Demo is marked alive and video present.
impact_rationale: Movie-watchers have a clear recurring discovery and planning problem, and preserving personal control addresses a real frustration with generic chat recommendations.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies movie and TV viewers and concrete discovery/planning use cases.
creativity_rationale: The human-controlled, constraint-aware weekend lineup is a fresh synthesis of recommendation and planning rather than simple chat search.
creativity_evidence: Locks, not-for-me explanations, and partial lineup rebuild are distinctive interaction choices.
red_flags: End-to-end agent invocation and completed lineup were not visually verified.
standouts: Human remains in control of recommendations and lineup state.
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and meaningful WebMCP collaboration.

one_line: A shared visual investigation workspace for humans and agents.
what_it_does: Combines datasets, evidence, hypotheses, findings, relationships, and provenance on a canvas, exposing structured tools for querying, comparison, counterevidence, and causal reasoning.
leverage_rationale: The central value is shared live state: agents operate on the same visual investigation and provenance graph humans inspect. A general browser agent could not comparably and reliably maintain this structured investigative state.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 48 structured tools operating on the same workspace.
Tools cover querying, cohorts, outliers, evidence, hypotheses, counterevidence, findings, causal links, branching, and saved views.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious but coherent, with three example investigations and an auditable workflow; the lack of readable frame detail prevents a 9-10 claim.
execution_evidence: Packet states three complete example investigations.
Frame sheet visibly shows linked analytics visualizations and controls.
Demo is marked alive and video present.
impact_rationale: Investigators, analysts, and data teams have a concrete need to combine human sensemaking with scalable search and auditable evidence.
impact_evidence: Packet names checkout, ML-quality, and suspicious-activity investigations.
Visible dashboard shows plots, tables, and analysis panels.
creativity_rationale: A spatial, provenance-preserving investigation shared between a human and agent is a genuinely original interaction model pursued at substantial depth.
creativity_evidence: Canvas combines hypotheses, evidence, relationships, and agent actions rather than hiding reasoning in chat.
Competing hypotheses and counterevidence are explicit product primitives.
usability_note: Powerful but potentially complex for first-time users.
red_flags: Frame text is small, so exact tool invocation cannot be independently read.
standouts: Auditable shared investigation state and branching.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and originality with a credible analytical audience.

one_line: Deterministic CRM reliability auditing with human-agent co-review.
what_it_does: Scores a synthetic CRM, prioritizes data-quality issues, and lets an agent retrieve summaries, issue lists, and explanations while focusing the same evidence for the human.
leverage_rationale: Bounded structured read-only tools improve precision and shared focus, but the deterministic report itself is available without WebMCP and a general agent could inspect it with some friction.
leverage_evidence: Three named read-only tools expose summary, priority issues, and explanations.
Packet says agent-selected records are automatically focused and highlighted for the human.
Visible report shows a concrete 60.4 health score and ranked sections.
execution_rationale: The deterministic audit, score breakdown, prioritized queue, and synchronized review form a focused, apparently functional product; mutation or remediation is intentionally out of scope.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows CRM Health Doctor dashboard with score 60.4 and tables.
Demo marked alive; public repository present.
impact_rationale: CRM administrators and RevOps teams face exactly the data-quality failures targeted, and deterministic prioritization is credible value before agent automation.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies missing ownership, stale deals, weak activity signals, and malformed fields.
Audience explicitly includes CRM admins and RevOps.
creativity_rationale: Human-agent co-review of a deterministic CRM audit is a solid new angle, though the underlying diagnostic category is established.
creativity_evidence: Read-only co-review and synchronized row highlighting are concrete interaction choices.
usability_note: Focused report and read-only safety model should be approachable.
red_flags: Synthetic CRM data limits direct production validation.
standouts: Deterministic evidence instead of LLM guesses.
advance_reason: Strong execution and practical CRM use case.

one_line: Space-themed project and productivity mission control shared with an agent.
what_it_does: Manages project boards, flight plans, inbox captures, notes, milestones, mind maps, and workspaces, with agent tools that mutate live authenticated state.
leverage_rationale: The agent can perform structured cross-feature operations against the user's authorized live workspace and the human sees invalidated queries update in place; UI automation would be markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Thirteen tools include reading plans, creating/moving tasks, notes, milestones, captures, and search.
Packet describes row-level security and live query invalidation after mutations.
Frames show the mission-control and mission-board product surfaces.
execution_rationale: Many coherent productivity surfaces are presented and the live galaxy UI is visibly polished, but frame repetition weakens proof of completed mutations.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows consistent branded mission boards and mission-control screens.
Packet says demo alive and public repo present.
impact_rationale: Individuals and teams can benefit from a unified task, planning, notes, and capture workflow, especially when an agent handles repetitive organization.
impact_evidence: Packet lists concrete project-management workflows and shared workspaces.
creativity_rationale: The persistent galaxy/mission-control metaphor is memorable and the agent is integrated across a broad productivity model, beyond a chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Mission boards, flight plans, launch animation, inbox-to-task conversion, and mind maps form a distinctive system.
usability_note: Visually distinctive but dense and metaphor-heavy.
red_flags: Most frame-sheet panels repeat landing/product sections rather than showing a complete mutation.
standouts: Live shared state with authorization boundaries.
advance_reason: Broad, credible productivity integration with substantial WebMCP delta.

one_line: Design-system capture and governance for AI-generated websites.
what_it_does: Captures a site's visual rules into an interactive wiki, gives those rules to an agent, and checks generated pages against them.
leverage_rationale: Structured design-system extraction and validation changes the agent from generic page generator to constrained, checkable implementer; scraping a site with general automation would be less reliable and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes capture, interactive design wiki, generation, and strict governance.
Frame sheet visibly shows multiple generated site examples and builder-like screens.
execution_rationale: The visual outputs and design-wiki concept are clearly presented, but the frame evidence does not conclusively show a failed rule being rejected or a full capture-to-validation run.
execution_evidence: Nine gallery images and video are listed.
Frame sheet shows polished landing pages, dashboards, and design-system views.
impact_rationale: Teams shipping AI-generated sites have a real brand-consistency problem, and reusable machine-readable rules directly address it.
impact_evidence: Packet explains brand failures from agents lacking explicit standards.
Multiple branded output examples are visible.
creativity_rationale: Turning any reference site into an interactive, enforceable design wiki is a strong and memorable synthesis of design tooling and agent generation.
creativity_evidence: Design governance and explicit tell-it-no validation are central rather than cosmetic.
usability_note: Potentially powerful; capture and rule interpretation need careful UX.
red_flags: Validation behavior is claimed more strongly than visibly demonstrated.
standouts: Machine-readable design governance for AI output.
advance_reason: Strong concept and clear audience pain.

one_line: Visual editor that lets non-technical owners safely edit static websites.
what_it_does: Exposes shared editing operations to humans and agents: discover content, read and update text or links, inspect history, undo, and publish deliberately to canonical static files.
leverage_rationale: Constrained tools operate on the same editor state and history while withholding arbitrary DOM access; this is substantially more reliable and safe than UI driving for precise content edits.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies discover/read/update/history/undo tools and human-only publishing.
Frame sheet visibly shows selection outlines and an inspector in a visual editor.
execution_rationale: The editor interface and selection/inspector workflow are convincingly shown, but no frame clearly proves save/publish or an agent invocation.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows editable page, selected elements, scrolling, and properties panel.
Packet states shared editor core and static-file canonical publishing.
impact_rationale: Small organizations and site owners commonly need simple content changes without developer intervention; constrained editing reduces risk.
impact_evidence: Packet explicitly identifies non-technical owners of static sites and developer dependency.
creativity_rationale: A human-first visual editor reused as a safe agent surface is a thoughtful interaction model, though visual site editing is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Shared history and deliberate human publish boundary are notable design choices.
usability_note: Direct manipulation and inspector are familiar; publishing guardrail is clear.
red_flags: End-to-end edit-to-publish proof is absent from visible frames.
standouts: Agent and human share one constrained editing history.
advance_reason: Practical audience, strong safety model, and meaningful leverage.

one_line: Private, browser-local legal source library with agent-built support maps.
what_it_does: Lets lawyers save holdings with case-specific notes and have an agent search only saved sources to build maps separating excerpts, notes, and gaps.
leverage_rationale: The controlled tool surface preserves browser-local source-of-truth and prevents unsupported retrieval or invention; general chat upload or UI scraping would compromise the core workflow and trust boundary.
leverage_evidence: Two named tools capture sources and search/build maps from the saved library.
Packet explicitly says the agent must use the site's real tools and only saved material.
Local browser storage and no server upload are central constraints.
execution_rationale: The narrow workflow is well specified and the packet describes a concrete Spanish-language legal use case; video is present but detailed end-to-end states are not fully readable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a browser-based legal/research interface and workflow states.
Packet gives concrete case Ramírez example and source/note/gap separation.
impact_rationale: Lawyers need trustworthy, case-scoped research support and strong provenance; browser-local operation directly addresses confidentiality and hallucination concerns.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies a practicing Colombian lawyer audience and explicit rule that sources bound claims.
Concrete use case involves medicine access and EPS delay.
creativity_rationale: The source-decides-what-can-be-claimed model and private, case-by-case support map are unusually focused and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Separating excerpt, lawyer note, and gaps is a distinctive reasoning interaction.
Agent access is deliberately limited to saved holdings.
usability_note: Narrow workflow and provenance boundaries support trust; Spanish-first UI targets its audience.
red_flags: No legal accuracy validation beyond source-grounding is established.
advance_reason: Exceptional audience fit, impact, and originality.

one_line: Rule-checked room planner where agents propose and humans accept layouts.
what_it_does: Builds measured 2D/3D rooms, furniture, doors, and windows; agents inspect the same document and create separate proposals checked for clearances, routes, and spatial rules.
leverage_rationale: Structured geometry, constraints, and proposal state are central: a general agent cannot reliably infer exact dimensions, door swings, routes, and furniture relationships from pixels. WebMCP makes agent planning precise and reviewable.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 16 native tools, shared document state, separate Proposal versus Yours, and a rule engine.
Rules include door swings, clearances, routes, TV/seating, table gaps, and bed-side constraints.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent local-first model, explicit proposal/apply/discard boundaries, 2D/3D views, and domain-specific validation; packet and frame evidence indicate a mature central workflow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows geometry/room-planning views and staged layouts.
Packet states measured input, proposal generation, rule checking, and human-only apply.
Demo marked alive and video present.
impact_rationale: Home planners, designers, and people fitting existing furniture have a real spatial planning need, and rule-checked alternatives offer concrete value.
impact_evidence: Packet names measured rooms, owned furniture, walking routes, and comparison of proposals.
creativity_rationale: Separating agent proposals from the accepted human layout while checking real-world spatial rules is an ambitious and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Proposal/Yours split and human-only apply are distinctive.
Domain rule engine goes well beyond collision-free rectangles.
usability_note: Clear review boundary, though room-planning rule density may require onboarding.
red_flags: Live agent call text is not fully legible in the frame sheet.
standouts: Precise, safe agent proposals for spatial design.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage with strong execution and impact.

one_line: Browser-local volumetric medical imaging reading room with privacy-preserving agent tools.
what_it_does: Loads local or de-identified NIfTI studies, renders CT/MRI volumes, and lets an agent describe studies, find bright regions, focus views, change layout, and export approved findings.
leverage_rationale: The agent receives structured measurements and controls a shared visual reading room without the scan leaving the browser; pixel/DOM-driving cannot provide comparable reliable volumetric navigation or privacy boundary.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies five tools and says the agent never receives the scan.
Human-visible overlays update while tool responses contain measurements/metadata.
Export requires explicit human approval.
execution_rationale: A focused viewer, local data path, NiiVue rendering, structured tools, and approval-gated export form a coherent workflow. Clinical-grade correctness is not established, so this is not a 9-10.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows loaded brain volume views, crosshairs, and supporting panels.
Packet states local NIfTI loading, de-identified demo, and WebGPU/WebGL2 viewer.
impact_rationale: Radiology and clinical imaging workflows have a serious privacy and navigation problem; local processing and structured assistance offer credible value even for a niche audience.
impact_evidence: Packet directly addresses hospitals' reluctance to upload patient scans.
Visible medical imaging viewer demonstrates the intended domain.
creativity_rationale: Combining browser-local volumetric imaging, agent navigation, and approval-gated findings is an ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent gets measurements/metadata without receiving the scan.
Shared overlays and human approval preserve clinical control.
usability_note: Privacy and approval boundaries are strong; medical viewer complexity is inherently high.
red_flags: Not evidence of clinical validation or diagnostic safety.
Exact tool calls are not fully legible in frames.
standouts: Privacy-preserving agent assistance for volumetric scans.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and impact with a credible technical boundary.
